status: investigation only; no production voice, model, prompt or deployment change

budget.note: The app ledger charges the full $0.125 Live reservation when no /api/live/turn usage is reported. The increase is conservative and overstates actual provider usage.

scope.notes: Direct API key testing bypassed the app token voice lock. App-level samples used the production token endpoint.

notes: 2.5 Native has consistently wider pitch movement: neutral 5.30 vs 3.47 semitones, current prompt 4.82 vs 3.50, tour-long 5.58 vs 3.78, tour-short 5.95 vs 4.54.
Frame-to-frame pitch movement is also more than double on 2.5: 1.27–1.72 semitones vs 0.60–0.99 on 3.8. This is a closer proxy for moment-to-moment liveliness than overall range.
2.5 Native first audio is 2.8–4.0s slower in like-for-like captures: neutral 4.1s vs 1.3s; current prompt 4.9s vs 1.4s; tour-long 6.2s vs 2.2s; tour-short 5.1s vs 1.4s.
2.5 Native streams ~44ms chunks vs ~350ms on 3.8 Live. More granular, but more messages and more scheduling overhead.
2.5 Native peaks at 0 dBFS in several samples; 20 clipped samples total across the 2.5 set. Add headroom or a soft limiter before playback.
Affective dialogue on 2.5 did not consistently increase measured pitch/energy variation in the one EN/FR pair. Subjective listening is required.

notes: The current prompt makes the opening ~30% longer (14.9s vs 11.5s), reduces energy variation (5.42 dB vs 7.30 dB) and slightly reduces frame-to-frame pitch movement (0.603 vs 0.648 semitones) without increasing overall pitch variation.
The current prompt produced one incorrect self-reference: 'your independent AI-powered portfolio guide' instead of Nour's assistant.
Long tour opening: 18.6s average, 4.8 disclaimer terms per 100 words. Transcripts reproduce 'live, interactive, personalized', 'interrupt', 'navigate' and 'stop at any time' almost verbatim.
The short opening also raises frame-to-frame pitch movement on Iapetus from 0.596 to 0.782 semitones (+31%).
Short tour opening: 7.9s average, zero disclaimer terms. Refined Sadachbia opening: 6.4s average, 4.63 semitones, zero disclaimer terms.
The same long/short effect appears on Iapetus and Sadachbia, so it is a prompt effect, not a voice effect.

Appending a delivery block to the 30k-character prompt did not consistently improve prosody and made responses longer (20.8s EN / 21.5s FR). Trimming the opening is more effective than adding another rule.

evidence: App-level Iapetus samples: pitch variation 3.50–3.53 semitones, first audio 1.30–1.65s. Direct 3.8 Iapetus: 3.47 neutral / 3.50 current, first audio 1.27–1.35s. Playback preserves the flat prosody rather than creating it.
App chunk arrival gaps reached 159ms (Puck) and 190ms (Iapetus); scheduled underruns were zero in the measured runs because the previous chunk covered the gap.
Direct 3.8 chunks average ~350ms; 2.5 chunks average ~44ms. One direct 3.8 sample had a 2ms scheduled gap; no overlap or clipping in 3.8.
Output PCM is 24 kHz, mono, 16-bit; base64 decoding is correct on little-endian browsers. No pitch/speed shift measured.

issues.detail: downsampleTo16k uses naive decimation without an anti-alias low-pass filter. Mic audio above 8kHz folds back into the speech band, degrading ASR/VAD.
issues.fix: Use an AudioWorklet resampler or a low-pass filter plus interpolation; test on 44.1k and 48k devices.

issues.detail: createScriptProcessor(4096) is deprecated and adds ~85ms input buffering at 48kHz, plus processing latency.
issues.fix: Move mic capture to AudioWorklet with 128–256 frame blocks; keep a small ring buffer.

issues.detail: playAudio schedules each chunk at nextPlayTime with no jitter buffer or crossfade. A late chunk resets playback to now, creating an audible gap/click. Fine on the test network, fragile on mobile/Bluetooth.
issues.fix: Keep 150–300ms of lead, crossfade 5–10ms at chunk boundaries, and avoid resetting the clock for small lateness.

issues.detail: playAudio hardcodes 24000 when creating buffers and ignores inlineData.mimeType. Correct for current Gemini output, but breaks silently if the provider changes rate.
issues.fix: Parse the mimeType rate and validate 16-bit alignment.

issues.detail: stopPlayback stops sources immediately with no gain ramp; interruption can click.
issues.fix: Ramp gain to zero over 20–30ms before stopping.

issues.detail: No AudioContext.resume() on visibility/user gesture, no device-change handling, and a forced 24kHz output context. Bluetooth headsets may switch to HFP and resample to 8/16kHz.
issues.fix: Resume on gesture/visibility; use the device default rate and a worklet ring buffer; test iOS/Safari, Chrome/Android and Bluetooth.

issues.detail: 2.5 Native output reached 0 dBFS with 20 clipped samples across the set; 3.8 peaked around -2.3 dBFS average.
issues.fix: Apply -3dB safety gain or a soft limiter in the output path.

current.tools: portfolio, knowledge and presentation function declarations

supportedLevers: realtimeInputConfig.automaticActivityDetection: start/end sensitivity, prefixPaddingMs, silenceDurationMs (documented for Live).
generationConfig temperature/topP/topK: accepted by the SDK and by 3.8 in two test samples; effect on voice prosody was small and noisy (5.57/5.32 vs 5.24 semitones). Do not treat as a primary fix.
proactivity and enableAffectiveDialog only on 2.5; do not send them to 3.8.
speechConfig voiceName is the strongest supported voice lever.
notSupportedOrNotRecommended: languageCode for native audio (auto language selection).
TTS-specific controls presented as Live controls.

recommendations.change: Test Sadachbia as the production voice on 3.8 Live, with Zubenelgenubi as the English alternative and Achird as the warmer/darker alternative.
recommendations.evidence: Sadachbia: 4.63 semitones with the refined opening (5.24 with the slightly longer short opening), in both EN and FR; frame-to-frame movement 0.83–0.99; first audio ~1.4s. Iapetus: 3.47 / 0.60. Zubenelgenubi EN 5.61 but FR 3.75 and lower micro-movement. Achird has the lowest centroid (warmest) but lower variation.

recommendations.change: Replace the long tour opening with the refined 1–2 sentence opening.
recommendations.evidence: Opening length 18.6s -> 6.4s; disclaimer terms 4.8 per 100 words -> 0; same 3.8 model. Transcripts become 'Hi, I'm Nupa… What brings you to Nour's work today?' instead of listing interrupt/navigate/stop.

recommendations.change: Trim and deduplicate the live system prompt after the opening fix: keep identity, grounding, safety and a compact delivery block; move presentation protocol to a tour-start context message.
recommendations.evidence: ~30k characters and ~30 rules; identity, scope, grounding and question rules are duplicated. Tail-only addition did not fix prosody.

recommendations.change: Do not switch permanently to 2.5 Native without approval. If pursued, run a side-by-side tool-calling/presentation test and accept the 3–5s first-audio latency.
recommendations.evidence: 2.5 is more expressive (5.30 vs 3.47 neutral) but first audio 4.1s vs 1.3s; preview model with an uncertain retirement path; 2.5 output clips at 0 dBFS.

recommendations.change: Harden the audio pipeline: AudioWorklet mic capture with proper resampling, 150–300ms output jitter buffer, crossfades, gain ramp on interrupt, -3dB safety gain, resume/device-change handling.
recommendations.evidence: Naive decimation, ScriptProcessor, no jitter buffer, forced 24k output, no background recovery; measured app gaps up to 190ms but zero underruns on this network.

caveats: Objective metrics are proxies. Perceived warmth, gender, humour and trust require listening.
Current system prompt is reconstructed from source; the live token response omits systemInstruction, and DB persona/knowledge overrides may differ.
Each model/voice cell has one or two samples; treat differences as directional, not statistically stable.
App-level samples used the production token endpoint and are Iapetus only; the client voice override did not take effect.
Direct API spend is outside the app ledger (~$0.31 estimated); the app caps and ledger were not changed.
2.5 Native is a preview model; availability and behavior may change.
